description: From: Elixir Parity. Finding (2026-11-25): not an fz bug. OTP's json.erl breaks its own types. At json.erl:660, format_value passes fun(Value, Enc) -> UserEnc(Value, Enc, State) end to encode_atom; encode_atom calls it with itself as Enc, and the wrapper passes that 2-arity encoder() as formatter()'s Encoder argument, which json.erl:569 declares as a 3-arity formatter(). BEAM runs it only because format_value's binary clause ignores _Enc; dialyzer does not check calls through fun variables (probes fz-otp-json/probes/mue73/m.erl, o.erl pass; n.erl, a direct contract break, is flagged). fz resolves user_enc to &format_value/3 and refuses the call as a provable spec violation; the closure's arity is carried correctly (p2.fz: a 1-arity closure to a spec'd 2-arity callback is refused). User decision: fix the type in the port: formatter()'s Encoder :: formatter() | encoder(), listed as a known deviation from OTP; the code is unchanged (JSON owns the port). No fz change.
title: A closure passed where a 3-arity callback spec is declared is typed by its own arity
